title: Cap. III Rat. 4: optimum modus — glory by merits foresight as crown of justice
latin: Rat. 4. Aequum est ut statuamus Deum optimo modo homines ad gloriam designare: Sed optimus modus est ex praevisione meritorum id facere: sic enim decernitur tanquam corona Justitiae.
pass_a: Reason 4. It is fair that we should establish that God designates men to glory in the best mode: But the best mode is to do that from foresight of merits: for thus it is decreed as a crown of Justice.
pass_b: Rat. 4. It is fair to hold that God marks people out for glory in the best way. But that best way, they say, is to do it from foresight of merits — for so the decree is cast as a crown of justice.

lemmas.gloss: best mode of designating to glory

title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 4: not optimum — strips pure mercy; Detur totum Deo; Cyprian
latin: Sol. Deum optimo modo omnia facere, nemo nisi pessimus audet negare: sed negamus tamen optimum modum eligendi homines ad vitam aeternam esse illum, qui nititur praescientia meritorum. Non est optimus, quia non optime facit ad illustrandam gloriam purae misericordiae Divinae erga electos. Nam tollit illud quod Augustinus passim inculcat, Detur totum Deo. Tollit etiam illud Cypriani, ab Augustino nunquam satis laudatum, In nullo gloriandum; quia nihil est nostrum.
pass_a: Solution. That God does all things in the best mode, no one except the worst dares deny: but we deny nonetheless that the best mode of electing men to eternal life is that which rests on foresight of merits. It is not the best, because it does not best serve to illustrate the glory of the pure divine mercy toward the elect. For it takes away that which Augustine everywhere inculcates, Let the whole be given to God. It also takes away that of Cyprian, never enough praised by Augustine, In nothing is one to glory; because nothing is ours.
pass_b: Sol. That God does all things in the best way no one but the worst would deny — yet we deny that the best way of electing people to eternal life is the one that rests on foresight of merits. It is not best, because it does least to display the glory of God’s pure mercy toward the elect. It strips what Augustine everywhere presses: Let the whole be given to God. It also strips Cyprian’s line, which Augustine never praised enough: In nothing is one to glory, because nothing is ours.

lemmas.gloss: glory of pure mercy toward elect

lemmas.lemma: Detur totum Deo / In nullo gloriandum

title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 4: pride; impossible in sin — efficacious grace only to predestined
latin: Porro, non est optimus modus eligendi, quia hominem inflat superbia, dum supponit unumquemque suis operibus semet a non-electis discrevisse. Demum addo, tantum abest ut sit optimus, ut ne possibilis quidem sit in hoc statu peccati. In homine enim per peccatum corrupto nulla possunt praesciri merita ad vitam aeternam efficacia, nisi Deus gratuito illa dederit. Deus nulli dat talia, nisi cui decrevit dare ab aeterno. Nemini decrevit dare gratiam efficacem ad salutem, nisi illis quos praedestinavit ad salutem. A primo igitur ad ultimum, merita talium non possunt praevideri in nondum electis ad vitam aeternam: Non igitur ex praescientia meritorum praecedente ad vitam eliguntur.
pass_a: Further, it is not the best mode of electing, because it inflates a man with pride, while it assumes that each one by his own works has distinguished himself from the non-elect. Finally I add, it is so far from being the best that it is not even possible in this state of sin. For in a man corrupted by sin no merits efficacious to eternal life can be foreknown, unless God has freely given them. God gives such to no one except him to whom he decreed to give from eternity. To no one did he decree to give efficacious grace unto salvation except to those whom he predestined unto salvation. From first to last, therefore, the merits of such cannot be foreseen in those not yet elected to eternal life: They are not therefore elected to life from a preceding foresight of merits.
pass_b: Further, it is not the best mode of electing, because it puffs a person up with pride by assuming each has by his own works set himself apart from the non-elect. Finally: it is so far from best that it is not even possible in this state of sin. In a person corrupted by sin no merits efficacious for eternal life can be foreknown unless God has freely given them. God gives those only to whom he decreed from eternity to give. He decreed efficacious grace unto salvation only to those he predestined to salvation. From first to last, then, such merits cannot be foreseen in those not yet elected to eternal life — so they are not elected to life from a preceding foresight of merits.

lemmas.gloss: not even possible in state of sin

title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 4: Jesuits vs other Pontificii — Mary/Apostles absolute; Valentia
latin: Sed illud etiam adjungamus, Jesuitas hunc ab aliis Pontificiis diffidere; qui virginem Mariam, beatos Apostolos, aliosque eximie sanctos, ad gloriam absolute praedestinatos docent ante omnem praescientiam meritorum: Verisimile autem est optimos fuisse optimo modo praedestinatos. De illis igitur eximie sanctis sic scribit Valentia, Tales ante respectum Divinae praescientiae ad finalem eorum cooperationem, praedestinantur ad vitam aeternam, In 1. qu. 23. Sed linquamus Jesuitas compugnantes:
pass_a: But let us also add this, that the Jesuits differ on this from other Pontificians; who teach that the virgin Mary, the blessed Apostles, and other eminently holy ones, were absolutely predestined to glory before all foresight of merits: And it is probable that the best were predestined in the best mode. Of those eminently holy ones, therefore, Valentia writes thus: Such, before the regard of the divine foresight to their final cooperation, are predestined to eternal life, On 1. q. 23. But let us leave the Jesuits fighting among themselves:
pass_b: Add also: the Jesuits themselves diverge here from other Roman doctors, who teach that the virgin Mary, the blessed Apostles, and other eminently holy persons were absolutely predestined to glory before any foresight of merits — and it is likely the best were predestined in the best way. Of those eminently holy ones Valentia writes: such are predestined to eternal life before any regard of God’s foresight to their final cooperation (In 1. q. 23). But leave the Jesuits fighting one another:

title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 4 close: gratuitous election stands; crown as prize; foresight after
latin: et illud denique respondeamus, Eligi posse homines gratuito ad vitam aeternam, quamvis corona vitae aeternae decernatur electis imponenda, ut premium vitae laudabiliter justeque transactae. Nam voluntas Dei de modo perducendi ad premium per opera sanctitatis, non evertit gratuitam et misericordem electionem ad vitam aeternam ex proposito primario et beneplacito mero eligentis. Quando enim Deus decernit perducere aliquem ad gloriam per talia opera, primarium decretum dandi gloriam non oritur ex praevisione illorum operum, sed ex hoc decreto fluit voluntas dandi gratiam efficacem ad talia opera justitiae facienda. Illorum igitur praevisio electione posterior.
pass_a: and finally let us answer this, That men can be elected gratuitously to eternal life, although the crown of eternal life is decreed to be set upon the elect as a prize of a life laudably and justly spent. For the will of God concerning the mode of bringing them to the prize through works of holiness does not overturn the gratuitous and merciful election to eternal life from the primary purpose and mere good pleasure of the one electing. For when God decrees to bring someone to glory through such works, the primary decree of giving glory does not arise from foresight of those works, but from this decree flows the will of giving efficacious grace for doing such works of justice. Their foresight, therefore, is posterior to election.
pass_b: and finally: people can be elected gratuitously to eternal life even when the crown of eternal life is decreed to be set on the elect as the prize of a life lived laudably and justly. God’s will about the way of bringing them to that prize through holy works does not overturn gratuitous, merciful election to eternal life from the elector’s primary purpose and mere good pleasure. When God decrees to bring someone to glory through such works, the primary decree to give glory does not rise from foresight of those works — rather, from that decree flows the will to give efficacious grace for doing such works of justice. So foresight of them is after election.

lemmas.gloss: gratuitous election with crown as prize
primary purpose and mere good pleasure
